title: Eleven Nights and One Heavy Fold
subtitle: 戏剧表演 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）
meta: 主题语境：戏剧表演（文学艺术与体育·戏剧与表演）　|　核心词汇：curtain　|　正文 338 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 curtain 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1947 the stage manager ① drew a curtain that no company in the city would have risked, and he said the drawing was the whole of the opening. The ② curtain, meaning the cloth and not the ending, ran eleven nights and stayed unwashed; a curtain, he said, is the only thing in a theatre that is judged by how long it is left hanging.

Every ③ curtain in that house had the same heavy fold against it, and the ④ curtain at the end, meaning the one they kept for the last act and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever applauded twice. A curtain, the prompter said, is nine parts timing and one part somebody willing to pull; the manager said the pulling is the part that fills eleven nights.

The playwright meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the curtain was the whole of the evening, meaning the close and not the cloth. The ⑥ curtain, meaning the close and not any of that, is the only thing in an evening that everybody waits for and nobody wants; curtain, she said, is either something you draw or the only word that means both a cloth and a close. She said the close is the part they remember.

By 1954 the ⑦ curtain had become a line in a contract, and the contract had become an argument about the heavy fold. The ⑧ curtain of the whole thing, the manager wrote in May, was one theatre and eleven nights of pulling; curtain, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to pull. She said the pulling was never mentioned.

The ⑨ curtain I remember is the one at the end, which fell in 1962 and is still described as the slowest in the city. A ⑩ curtain, the prompter said in 1964, is the only thing that improves by being waited for; every curtain, she said, is a close that has agreed to look like a cloth. She said the close was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 幕；帷幕（指舞台上挂着的那一道）
B. n. 幕（指那块布本身，与那个结尾相对）
C. 固定搭配：draw a curtain 拉（开）帷幕
D. n. 幕（指留给最后一幕用的那一道）
E. n. 幕；帷幕（抽象总称，指一整座剧院的开合）
F. n. 幕（指合同里写到、被约定的那一道）
G. n. 落幕；终场（指一晚演出的收束）
H. n. 落幕（抽象总称，指众人等待的那个结束）

items.q: drew a curtain that no company in the city would have risked
The curtain, meaning the cloth and not the ending
the curtain was the whole of the evening
the curtain had become a line in a contract
The curtain of the whole thing
A curtain, the prompter said in 1964

answers.why: draw a curtain 意为“拉（开）帷幕”，1947 年舞台监督拉开了一道全城没有一家剧团敢冒险的帷幕。
curtain 意为“幕”，指那块布本身而不是那个结尾，它挂了十一个晚上从未洗过。
curtain 意为“幕”，指那座剧院里每一道帷幕，每一道都有同一道厚重的褶子。
curtain 意为“幕”，指留给最后一幕用的那一道，是唯一有人为之鼓过两次掌的。
curtain 意为“落幕、终场”，指一晚演出的收束，剧作家说落幕就是那一晚的全部。
curtain 意为“落幕”，指众人等待的那个结束而不是别的，是一晚演出里人人都等、却无人想要的东西。
curtain 意为“幕”，指合同里写到、被约定的那一道，到 1954 年这道幕成了合同里的一行。
curtain 意为“幕、帷幕”，监督五月写道，整件事的帷幕是一座剧院和十一个夜晚的拉幕。
curtain 意为“落幕”，我记得的是末尾那一次，1962 年落下，至今仍被说成全城最慢的一次。
curtain 为抽象总称，提词人 1964 年说，一道帷幕是唯一会因为被等待而变得更好的东西。
